title: Properties of Alkanes Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A gas stove flame, a burning candle and a tank of petrol all run on alkanes, yet one is a gas, one a solid and one a liquid. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 9, Hydrocarbons) Diya spots it in her kitchen, and we find out how alkanes behave and how they react.

On the molecule bench, chains grow carbon by carbon and their van der Waals pulls add up, so the boiling point rises (C1 to C4 gases, C5 to C17 liquids, C18 and above solids). Pentane morphs into 2-methylbutane and 2,2-dimethylpropane as the boiling point falls from 309.1 K to 300.9 K to 282.5 K. Then free radical halogenation of methane link by link, with electrons moving on curved arrows (initiation, propagation, termination), the heat from burning 8 g of methane (445 kJ), controlled oxidation, isomerisation, aromatisation, reaction with steam and pyrolysis, the exam trap, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 90 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

In this video:
0:00 Gas, liquid, solid: one family
0:30 The noodle rule: chain length and boiling point
1:05 Branching on the molecule bench
1:59 Pause and think: hexane or a branched isomer?
2:13 Free radical halogenation, link by link
3:11 Worked example: heat from burning methane
3:46 Controlled oxidation, isomerisation, aromatisation, steam, pyrolysis
4:29 Exam trap: chlorination gives a mixture
4:50 Practice question (NEET pattern)
5:23 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Conformations of Ethane. Can a molecule change its shape without breaking a single bond?
